newsitem.title: UK: Daley says U.S.-Japan trade tension not yet high.
newsitem.headline: Daley says U.S.-Japan trade tension not yet high.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said on Wednesday that trade tensions between the U.S. and Japan were not high yet but he still wanted to see greater access to the Japanese market.
"We don't think trade tension is that great at this moment but the trade gap is growing," he told Reuters Financial Television.
"In many areas, we still believe that the market is closed or at least very difficult to get into," he said.
"If the deficit continues to grow and it is felt that the Japanese economy is being improved by big increases in imports (to the U.S. and Europe), there will be a political reaction," he said.

Sticking to the trade theme, Daley said he was extremely disappointed at the level of U.S. exports to China. He was looking forward to new proposals from China regarding access to its markets that are "markedly different" to those he had seen so far.
Daley also said he expected President Bill Clinton to press for fast track authority to negotiate the expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement.
"I think it will be a difficult battle (to get it through Congress) but I expect the President to prevail.
"It's merely the ability to reach an agreement that then has to be brought back to Congress anyway."
A new report on NAFTA due soon will outline the "enormous successes as well as the problems of NAFTA so far," he said.
